title: Path Operations & HTTP Methods
summary: Map HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) to FastAPI route decorators.

sections.content: FastAPI provides decorators for all standard HTTP methods. Each maps directly to the corresponding HTTP verb:

items: POST = create, GET = read, PUT/PATCH = update, DELETE = delete
PUT = full replace (client sends all fields), PATCH = partial update

sections.title: FastAPI's 422
sections.content: FastAPI uses 422 (Unprocessable Entity) for validation errors, not 400. This is the default behavior when request data fails Pydantic validation.
FastAPI also supports OPTIONS (for CORS preflight) and HEAD (headers-only responses). These are less commonly used directly but are part of the HTTP spec.

code_challenge.title: CRUD Route Stubs
code_challenge.description: Create a FastAPI app with all 5 CRUD route stubs for /items. GET / should return a welcome message.
hints: POST doesn't need a request body to return 200 — just return a dict
All routes can return {} for now — they're stubs

quiz.question: Which HTTP method should you use to create a new resource?
quiz.explanation: POST is for creating new resources. The data for the new resource goes in the request body.

quiz.question: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
options: PUT replaces fully, PATCH updates partially
quiz.explanation: PUT is a full replacement (client sends all fields), PATCH is a partial update (client sends only changed fields).

quiz.question: What status code does FastAPI return for validation errors?
quiz.explanation: FastAPI returns 422 Unprocessable Entity when request data fails Pydantic validation. This is its default behavior.

quiz.question: Which URL pattern is recommended for REST APIs?
quiz.explanation: Use plural nouns (/items) without verbs. The HTTP method already indicates the action — no need to repeat it in the URL.

quiz.question: What status code should a successful POST (create) return?
quiz.explanation: 201 Created is the appropriate status code for successful resource creation via POST.
